title: Six ways to make drinking water safe: sand filters, chlorine, clay pot filters, solar bottles, folded cloth and straw filters

facts.text: By the early 1800s, slow sand filtration was beginning to be used regularly in Europe.
Communities and households can build effective slow sand or biosand filters from simple sand and gravel.
In 1908, chlorine was first used as a primary disinfectant of drinking water in Jersey City, New Jersey.
Household bleach (sodium hypochlorite) is the main disinfectant promoted by CDC and WHO for treating water at home.
Unlike sunlight (UV) treatment, chlorine leaves a residual that helps keep stored water from being contaminated again.
The clay pot filter was first developed in Guatemala by Fernando Mazariegos of the research institute ICAITI.
Clay is mixed with sawdust; when the pot is fired, the sawdust burns away and leaves a network of fine pores.
For solar disinfection, clear plastic bottles are laid on their side in sunlight for at least 6 hours.
In cloudy weather, solar disinfection needs 2 days in a row; very muddy water must be cleared first because particles block UV light.
In a field trial in rural Bangladesh (September 1999 to July 2002), villagers filtered water through old sari cloth folded four to eight times.
Filtering through folded sari cloth reduced cholera by 48% compared with the control villages.
The folded cloth removes tiny plankton (copepods) to which cholera bacteria attach.
Portable microfilters (including straw-type filters) with pores under 1 micrometer remove bacteria and protozoa.
Microfilters do not reliably remove viruses, which are much smaller than bacteria.

notes: 混合題 mixed-advanced-02 第 2 組用（2026-10-09 線上查證，只取事實、不取原句）。選文 E 的「about half as many cholera cases」對應 48% 的降幅；「three-year study」對應 1999 年 9 月到 2002 年 7 月。吸管濾水器只寫一般微過濾器的特性（CDC），不寫特定品牌與年份。陶壺濾水器的年份來源不一，選文不寫。
